q3.text:
Q3. Pointer actions

A Skipped or Failed reason that a different tool or a pack fixes ends with one secondary button that names the destination, such as 'Install script pack'.

Opening a tool keeps the files open and selects that tool in the rail. Installing a pack never retries automatically: the files stay in the list for a new run.

Retry appears only after a wrong password, a timeout or a processing error.

save.text:
Save step

Tools that combine many files into one always open the native save dialog. Toolbox draws no dialog of its own, so the sheet on the Merge board is a placeholder for the system one. It proposes 'lease-agreement-merged.pdf' in the output location.

If the chosen name already exists, Toolbox writes 'lease-agreement-merged-1.pdf' instead, and the result row says so: 'Renamed to avoid replacing lease-agreement-merged.pdf'.

row4.text: PDF Editor: one document, like a viewer

editor.text:
PDF Editor model

One document per window, like Preview or Acrobat. Page thumbnails sit on the left, the page in the middle, and the inspector for the chosen tool on the right.

The edit toolbar is always visible: Organize, Crop, Edit text, Add text, Sign, Fill forms, Marks, Redact, plus More for Flatten, Split, Merge, Bates, Details and opening the Files view.

Edits are a list of changes that you can undo. The original file is never changed. Export a copy writes a new file and is disabled until something changes.

edkeys.text:
PDF Editor keyboard and screen reader

F6 cycles between the toolbar, thumbnails, page and inspector. The toolbar and thumbnail strip use arrow keys, with Home and End.

Every mark on the page is a focusable object with a name, such as 'Text box, Signed on 12 October, page 3'. Arrow keys nudge it, Shift+arrow moves it further, and Delete removes it.

Undo and Redo announce what they changed, such as 'Undid Add text'.

export.text:
Export order and redaction

Export applies changes in a fixed order: fill forms, edit text, overlays, flatten, then redact.

Before a redacted export, the disclosure says what happens. Affected pages become 300 dpi images. Metadata, XMP and attachments are removed. Annotations, form fields and layers on those pages are removed.

A signature is typed or an uploaded picture. It is not a digital signature, and the Sign panel says so.

conv.text:
One file from many

Images to PDF, Merge, Create GIF, App Icon Set, combining a TIFF and Formatted PDF all make one output. Their run button ends in an ellipsis and opens the native save dialog.

Tools that make one file per input use 'Save to' with an example name. A clash gets -1, -2 and so on, and errors stay per file.

row10.text: Settings, packs, shortcuts and the app icon

set.text:
Settings

Settings opens with Cmd/Ctrl+, from anywhere and replaces the tool rail with its sections. Changes save immediately; there is no Save button.

Switches are real switches with labels. Every section is reachable with Tab and arrow keys.

Packs never download without asking. A tool that needs a missing pack names it and its size, then sends you to this screen or installs it in place.

sec1.text:
Lock & Unlock: mode and passwords

The view is File Security and its one tool is Lock & Unlock, so the rail never reads File Security twice. Unlock also removes restrictions from PDFs that open without a password, with no password needed, and saves an unlocked copy.

Lock and Unlock is a segmented control in the header. Switching keeps the file list, clears both password fields and re-checks every row for the new mode. It is disabled while a batch runs.

The batch password sits at the top of the options with show/hide. Lock adds Confirm under it. A mismatch marks Confirm as invalid with 'Passwords don't match. Type the new password again.' and Run names the reason.

A row's own password opens an inline editor in that row, with Confirm in Lock. Saved rows show 'Own password' with Change and Use batch password. Clearing it shows a status line with Undo.

sec2.text:
Lock & Unlock: intake, flags and results

Files the other mode accepts stay in the list, flagged with a reason and a Won't run tag, such as a .doc in Lock. A banner offers one action to remove every flagged file. Files no mode accepts go under 'N items not added'.

Results use the shared row pattern. Locked or unlocked rows open or show the copy. A warning row says what changed, such as a removed signature or a -1 rename. Skipped rows say why and point to the fix, such as Unlock it first. Failed rows say why and whether the file is fine.

Retry appears only for a wrong password (Try another password, with an inline field) or a processing error. It runs only that file. A missing PDF helper fails PDFs only, and Office files still run.

Show all in Finder or File Explorer opens the destination once for many results.

sec3.text:
Lock & Unlock: local, destination, search

A note in the options says the tool runs on this device with no network, and that passwords are never saved and are cleared on a mode switch or on leaving. Results repeat that passwords were cleared.

Save to defaults to next to each original. Change for this run shows This run only and Reset to default. Copies end in -protected or -unlocked, and nothing is replaced.

Command center: File Security, lock icon. Find a tool matches lock, unlock, protect, password, encrypt and decrypt.

New patterns: the mode segmented control, inline row editors, and flagged rows with a Won't run tag.

row1.text: Finding a tool, adding files, choosing where outputs go

row2.text: Running a batch and reading the results

q8.text:
Q8. Six views and rail scaling

The command center lists the six views as sections with their tools inline. Any tool is one click away, and search is focused with Cmd/Ctrl+K.

Inside a view, the app sidebar becomes that view's tool rail. It's a plain vertical list that scrolls, so 12 or more tools fit without truncation. Short names come from the registry.

Below 980 px the rail turns into a horizontal strip under the header. Tools that don't fit go into a More menu. Arrow keys, Home and End work in both layouts.

q5.text:
Q5. Intake

With no files, the whole center pane is the drop target. Its border becomes solid and its text reads 'Drop to add' while files are dragged over it. Open files is the primary button, with the shortcut beside it. The accepted types are listed under it.

Files that aren't added are collected in a 'Not added' group under the list, each with its reason. A folder, a duplicate and a wrong type each get their own line. A wrong type can point to the right tool. Nothing in this group blocks the run.

q1.text:
Q1. Destination and per-run marking

'Save to' sits in the options panel, just above the Run button, and is always visible. The default reads 'Next to each original' or names the folder.

Change for this run opens the native folder dialog. The changed line gets a 'This run only' badge and a Reset to default link. Leaving the view clears it.

If the folder is missing or can't be written, a dialog appears before anything runs. It offers 'Choose another folder' or 'Save next to originals'. An example output name sits beside the destination line.

q4.text:
Q4. Passwords and overrides

One masked field covers the whole batch. It has a show/hide eye and the note 'Never saved'.

A file with its own password shows a key badge, 'Own password', in the list's Password column. Every other file reads 'Batch password'. The override is set from the row's menu.

After a wrong password, the failed row opens an inline password field and Retry, so only that file runs again.

q7.text:
Q7. Shortcut hints

Hints appear only on the control they trigger, as a small key cap inside the button:
- Open files: Cmd/Ctrl+O
- Run: Cmd/Ctrl+Enter
- Find a tool: Cmd/Ctrl+K
- Settings: Cmd/Ctrl+,
- Cancel: Esc

List hints (Delete removes, Shift or Cmd/Ctrl-click selects) appear as one quiet line above the list once files are added.

All labels switch between Cmd and Ctrl, and between Finder and File Explorer, by platform. Use the Platform tweak on any screen to see both.

q6.text:
Q6. Progress, cancel, locked state

The batch strip at the top of the list shows 'Protecting 7 of 24'. Its bar fills one segment per finished file, coloured by result. Rows switch from Waiting to a spinner to their result as each file finishes, and finished outputs can be opened right away.

The options panel dims, with one line: 'Options are locked until the batch finishes'. The Run button becomes 'Cancel batch' (Esc).

Cancel asks first, saying what is kept and what won't run. Cancelled files become Skipped, with the reason 'Cancelled'.

q2.text:
Q2. Three-state rows and large batches

Each row has an icon, a word and a reason, so the state never depends on colour:
- Succeeded: a check.
- Skipped: a grey dash. It's a no-op, not a problem.
- Failed: a red cross.
Warnings are amber and sit under the output name.

The summary counts double as filters. In large batches, 'Needs attention' groups rows by reason, so 28 'Signature removed' rows become one group you can expand. The list keeps input order.

sr.text:
Screen-reader announcements

One polite live region sits on the batch strip:
- On start: 'Protecting 24 files.'
- During the run: progress every 5 files or 10 seconds, whichever is later, such as 'Protecting, 10 of 24 done.'
- On finish: 'Done. 21 protected, 2 skipped, 1 failed.' Focus stays where it was.

Each row is a list item whose accessible name reads as one sentence: file, state, reason, warnings, then output name. Row actions are real buttons, such as 'Open annual-report-protected.pdf'.

The cancel dialog traps focus and returns it to Cancel batch.

row13.text: PDF Conversion: PDF to EPUB and Formatted PDF

fq1.text:
Q1. Block formatting (Formatted PDF)

One toolbar above the document, nothing more: a block-type menu (Paragraph, Heading 1 to 3), Bold, Italic, bulleted and numbered list, then Table, Image… and Page break. There are no fonts, colours or alignment per block; the look comes from Page and Font in the right panel, so this stays a document builder, not a word processor.

Every toolbar button has a shortcut and shows it in its tooltip only. The document is a list of block cards with a type label in the gutter. The selected block gets a ring and Move up, Move down and Delete. Pasted text keeps paragraphs, headings, lists and bold or italic and drops the rest.

fq2.text:
Q2. Live preview (Formatted PDF)

The preview is the top of the right panel: one real-size page scaled to fit, with Page 1 of 2 and previous/next buttons. It redraws about half a second after typing stops. While it redraws, the old page dims and an Updating preview chip shows; the editor never waits for it.

When a settings section is open, the page shrinks so Page, Font, Header and footer and Title and author fit without scrolling. Text the app can't draw pauses the preview instead of showing wrong glyphs.

fq3.text:
Q3. Draft restore, discard and autosave (Formatted PDF)

There is one draft, kept in app data on this device. The toolbar status reads Draft saved on this device, or Saving draft… while writing. Opening the tool with a draft restores it and shows a quiet note with when it was saved, Discard draft… and Dismiss.

Discard draft… sits in the panel footer next to Save PDF… and asks in an alert dialog, with Keep editing focused and Esc to cancel. Discard says the draft can't be brought back and that images on disk are not touched. A successful save clears the draft; a failed save keeps it.

fq4.text:
Q4. Fonts used and platform note (Formatted PDF)

The font picker has two groups. Bundled with Toolbox lists the metric-compatible fonts, the same on every computer. On this computer lists system fonts, each tagged This computer only, with a line saying they can look slightly different on the other platform.

After saving, a Fonts used table shows what you chose, what went into the PDF and where it came from. A system font adds one platform note. A missing font, such as Calibri on a Mac, names the bundled substitute (Carlito) and says line breaks match. There is no platform note then, because bundled fonts are the same everywhere.

fq5.text:
Q5. Script-pack prompt (Formatted PDF)

Text outside Latin, Cyrillic and Greek is marked on its own block with a warning line. The preview pauses, and a note above the page names the script, says the pack is needed, and offers one Install script pack button with the 38 MB size. This is the same wording as Add text and the row patterns.

Save PDF… is disabled and the estimate says why: install the pack or remove that text. Nothing downloads until Install is chosen, and installing never saves on its own.

fq6.text:
Q6. EPUB options, reflow notes and Skipped rows

Options in order: Pages (All pages or a Range, using the shared syntax and clamp hints), Clean up (remove running headers, footers and page numbers, on by default), Cover (First page or No cover), Book details and Save to. Title and Author fields appear only when one PDF is in the list; for a batch, each book takes its details from its PDF.

Results keep Converted, Skipped and Failed rows in one list. Skipped is neutral and gives the reason (no text, range outside the PDF). Details open per row and list facts and notes: pages converted, images kept, where the table of contents came from, and content that couldn't reflow (two columns, tables, formulas, unreadable images) with page numbers.

fq7.text:
Q7. Scanned PDFs and OCR

A PDF with no text layer is Skipped, not Failed: There's no text to put in a book. It ends with one Open in OCR button, the shared pattern for a reason another tool fixes. Opening OCR keeps the files and selects OCR in the rail.

A PDF where only some pages have no text still converts. Its details list those pages and offer the same Open in OCR. Nothing runs OCR automatically.

fq8.text:
Q8. Destination and per-run change

PDF to EPUB uses the shared Save to row with an example name (the-long-road-home.epub, no suffix). Change… sets a folder for this run only, shown with a This run badge and Reset to default; it goes back to the default after the run. A clash gets -1, -2 and the row says Renamed to avoid replacing.

Formatted PDF makes one file, so Save PDF… ends in an ellipsis and opens the native save dialog. It starts in the last folder used by this tool, or Documents the first time, and suggests the title as the name. A name clash gets a number; nothing is replaced.

fq9.text:
Q9. Multi-select (PDF to EPUB)

The file list is a multi-select listbox: click, Shift-click for a range, Cmd-click (Ctrl-click on Windows) to add, Cmd+A (Ctrl+A) for all, Up and Down to move, Delete to remove. A quiet line above the list says this only while two or more rows are selected, next to Remove 2 selected with its Delete hint.

Options lock while converting; Esc cancels the batch after the current PDF.

Open questions: should Cmd+S also save in Formatted PDF? Are Ctrl+Alt heading keys safe with AltGr layouts? Are the bundled font names final? Should a save clear the draft, or keep it until the editor is reset?

fkeys.text:
Shortcuts, checked against the shell list (#429)

Formatted PDF, Mac (Windows):
Bold Cmd+B (Ctrl+B)
Italic Cmd+I (Ctrl+I)
Heading 1 to 3 Opt+Cmd+1 to 3 (Ctrl+Alt+1 to 3)
Paragraph Opt+Cmd+0 (Ctrl+Alt+0)
Bulleted list Shift+Cmd+8 (Ctrl+Shift+8)
Numbered list Shift+Cmd+7 (Ctrl+Shift+7)
Page break Shift+Cmd+Return (Ctrl+Shift+Enter)
Move block Opt+Shift+Up/Down (Alt+Shift+Up/Down)
Insert image Cmd+O (Ctrl+O), the shell's open key
Esc selects the block; then Delete removes it and Up/Down move between blocks
Undo and Redo as in PDF Editor
Save PDF… Cmd+Return (Ctrl+Enter), the shell's primary action

PDF to EPUB uses the batch keys: Cmd+Return converts, Esc cancels, Cmd+A, Delete, Up/Down.

No clash with Cmd+K, Cmd+comma, Cmd+/, Cmd+W, F6, Cmd+E, Cmd+D, Cmd+plus/minus/0 or Shift+Cmd+V.
